grounding.proposition: PASS=0 and FAIL=1 are categorical codes to enter in the concentration-max DMR field, not measured concentration magnitudes.
Pass/fail WET parameters use unit 9A (pass=0;fail=1) and carry no numeric LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR threshold.
Companion NOEC parameters in the same limit set report numeric percent limits (23%), not 0/1 pass/fail codes.
Observed FY reporting uses literal 0 with unit 9A, consistent with pass/fail coding rather than concentration.
Enter 1 when survival NOEC is below critical dilution (fail); otherwise enter 0 (pass).
Retest rows use the same 0/1 NOEC-versus-critical-dilution coding.
TOM3D/TOM6C require separate numeric NOEC concentration reporting, distinct from binary pass/fail entry.
Acute test failure is a toxicity-outcome determination at or below critical dilution, not arithmetic limit comparison.

remaining_uncertainty: Critical dilution magnitude is not stated in the retained structured rows. Four of twelve limit rows that share the PASS=0/FAIL=1 comment (TOM3D, TOM6C, TQM3D, TQM6C) are governed by separate numeric NOEC or coefficient-of-variation reporting instructions and must not be treated as binary 0/1 pass/fail parameters.
